title: Measuring Variable Importance Using Proportional Inclusive Marginal Effects
abstract: arXiv:2610.17053v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Shapley-based measures are widely used for measuring variable importance in statistics and machine learning. However, these measures have a serious issue--a nonactive variable can get a positive importance measure when it is correlated with an active variable. Herin et al. recently proposed a measure called proportional marginal effects (PME) that mitigates this spurious effect. However, PME is developed for deterministic models and has high computational cost. In this article, we propose a new measure called proportional inclusive marginal effects (PRIME) that overcomes these two limitations of PME. The key idea in PRIME is to use a novel model-free variable selection technique to identify the active variables and include only them in the computation of the importance measure. Analysis of test functions and real datasets show that PRIME can accurately and reliably quantify variable importance from noisy input-output data.

translated_title: 基于比例包含边际效应的变量重要性度量
translated_abstract: 基于Shapley的度量方法在统计学和机器学习中被广泛用于衡量变量重要性。然而，这些度量方法存在一个严重问题——当一个非活跃变量与活跃变量相关时，该非活跃变量可能获得正的重要性度量值。Herin等人最近提出了一种称为比例边际效应（PME）的度量方法来缓解这种虚假效应。然而，PME是为确定性模型开发的，且计算成本很高。本文提出了一种称为比例包含边际效应（PRIME）的新度量方法，克服了PME的这两个局限性。PRIME的关键思想是使用一种新颖的无模型变量选择技术来识别活跃变量，并仅将这些变量纳入重要性度量的计算中。对测试函数和真实数据集的分析表明，PRIME能够从含噪声的输入-输出数据中准确、可靠地量化变量重要性。
tldr: 提出了PRIME（比例包含边际效应）这一新的变量重要性度量方法，通过无模型变量选择技术仅纳入活跃变量进行计算，克服了PME仅适用于确定性模型且计算成本高的局限，能从含噪声数据中准确可靠地量化变量重要性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes PRIME (proportional inclusive marginal effects), a new variable importance measure that overcomes PME's limitations of being restricted to deterministic models and high computational cost by using a novel model-free variable selection technique to include only active variables, enabling accurate and reliable quantification of variable importance from noisy input-output data.
